lines.title: Horizontal three-phase separator
lines.text: This is a horizontal three-phase separator.

lines.title: Horizontal three-phase separator
lines.text: It takes the mixed stream from the wells and splits it into gas, oil or condensate, and water.

lines.title: Horizontal three-phase separator
lines.text: On a gas field, the liquid is mostly condensate and produced water.

lines.title: 1  Inlet diverter
lines.text: The well stream enters here and hits an inlet diverter.

lines.title: 1  Inlet diverter
lines.text: The sudden change in direction knocks most of the liquid out of the gas straight away.

lines.title: 1  Inlet diverter
lines.text: This is called bulk separation.

lines.title: 2  Gravity settling
lines.text: Gas flows along the top of the vessel.

lines.title: 2  Gravity settling
lines.text: It slows down in this large space, so heavier liquid droplets fall out under gravity.

lines.title: 3  Mist extractor
lines.text: Before the gas leaves, it passes through a mist extractor, usually a wire mesh pad or a vane pack.

lines.title: 3  Mist extractor
lines.text: It catches fine droplets that are too small to settle on their own.

lines.title: 4  Liquid retention
lines.text: Below, the liquid needs time.

lines.title: 4  Liquid retention
lines.text: Water is heavier, so it sinks to the bottom, while oil rises to the top.

lines.title: 4  Liquid retention
lines.text: That is why separators are sized for retention time: usually a few minutes, and longer for heavy or emulsified liquids.

lines.title: 5  The weir
lines.text: The oil layer floats on the water and spills over a weir into its own compartment.

lines.title: 5  The weir
lines.text: Water stays behind the weir and is drawn off from the bottom.

lines.title: 6  Control and protection
lines.text: Three control loops keep the vessel stable.

lines.title: 6  Control and protection
lines.text: A pressure controller on the gas outlet, a level controller on the oil compartment, and an interface level controller holding the oil water boundary.

lines.title: 6  Control and protection
lines.text: A pressure safety valve protects the vessel if pressure rises too far.

lines.title: Takeaway
lines.text: On a P and I D, find the inlet, the three outlets, the weir, and the three control loops.

lines.title: Takeaway
lines.text: Trace those, and you can read almost any separator.
